title: Opening Show
why: The only moment the whole competition is in one room, and where the villages, stages and plaza layout are explained. Everything after this assumes you were here.

title: Welcome and Introductions
why: Ten minutes that set up the Responsibility Conference she attends on all three days. Cheap, and the framing matters for the rest.
hook: Opens the conference on what responsible science owes communities as AI accelerates biological design.

title: The AI x Synthetic Biology Revolution
why: Fifteen minutes on what computational tools are doing to the field, from the village that would host our software work. Slip into Next-Gen Biomanufacturing at 10:15; it runs an hour and opens with introductions.
hook: How computational tools are changing work on biological systems, and how to join the village.

title: SynBio Oncology Knowledgebase: A tool from the Oncology Village
why: A village knowledgebase and how to join it. The mechanism is interesting for T4, the subject is not ours; dropped.
hook: A community hub for cancer-focused synthetic biology shares its knowledgebase and how to join.

title: The Role of Multidisciplinary Science to Address the Biggest Environmental Challenges
why: Our own village's framing talk. Runs against the Responsibility Conference opening and the OECD session; dropped.
hook: How AI, new materials, lab automation and sensing widen the use of biology against climate problems.

title: Next-Gen Biomanufacturing
why: The session hook names light-steered bioreactors. That is our machine, described by people who have taken it to production scale.
ask: At what working volume does light delivery stop being uniform, and what did you change first — the vessel geometry or the light source?
hook: Scaling biological production with robotics and light-steered bioreactors, plus what makes a company fundable.

title: Private Sector, Public Good? Building Accountability into the Bioeconomy
why: Run by the OECD with companies, investors and unions in the room, building an accountability roadmap. Ninety minutes of how a real institution is told to behave — the frame GEMS will be judged against long after this project.
ask: What does an accountability roadmap ask of a research group too small to have a compliance office?
hook: Companies, investors and unions work toward a roadmap for accountability in the commercial bioeconomy.

title: Rebuilding Translation: The PURE System and Where Cell-Free Biology Goes Next
why: Cell-free is the escape route if secretion stays blocked. Four blockers stand in front of secreted ACC deaminase; this panel skips all four.
ask: For a PLP-dependent oligomeric enzyme, does cell-free get you folded, active protein — or just protein?
hook: The cell-free PURE translation system from its first reconstitution to synthetic cell work today.

title: How Synbio is shaping Infectious Diseases Solutions
why: Outside our space. Listed to show the Friday morning slot was considered and spent elsewhere.
hook: A community village maps where synthetic biology addresses infectious disease, and the gaps that remain.

title: SynBio Alliance Showcase
why: Alliance members showing their work. Runs inside the OECD session, which is worth more; listed so the trade is visible.
hook: A showcase session where alliance members present the synthetic biology work they are doing.

title: The Importance of Art & Design in SynBio: What the iGEM Art & Design Village Is Working Towards
why: The art and design village's year in review. Not a track we are building this cycle; dropped.
hook: Meet the art and design community, review the year and consider what comes next.

title: SHIHAB: In Situ Biomanufacturing for Space Missions
relevance: same space
why: In-situ biomanufacturing under harder constraints than ours.
hook: Radiation-tolerant microbes and a compact bioreactor make therapeutic proteins on demand in space.
clash: Private Sector, Public Good? Building Accountability into the Bioeconomy

title: The Autonomous Lab: When Biology Runs Itself
why: The closed loop we claim in the digital twin, built by people who sell it.
ask: What does your trigger logic do with a sensor artefact? Ours put a 40% instrument drop into a real OD dip at 29 h.
hook: How software links instruments a lab already owns so experiments plan, run and read themselves.

title: Our Project: A Solution to Peach Tree Gummosis
relevance: direct competitor on chassis and on secretion; technique to borrow on fusion-protein secretion.
why: Plant disease in a woody crop — our problem in a different host.
hook: Field surveys and 3D-printed models shape a project against gummosis disease in peach trees.
clash: A PhD, a Start-Up, and a Career in Industry

title: A PhD, a Start-Up, and a Career in Industry
why: One route from PhD to industry, from someone engineering bacteria on waste gases. Useful to be able to describe to students who ask what this leads to.
hook: One route from PhD to industry, and what engineering bacteria that ferment waste gases involves.

title: From iGEM Project to Community Resource: Open Science for Lasting Impact
why: Exactly the question GEMS has not answered — how a project becomes something the community keeps using instead of a wiki that freezes in October — and it runs 11:50–12:05, five minutes into our judging session. Dropped, reluctantly. This is the one dropped session worth chasing the speaker for: the question below is the whole of track T4.
ask: What did you have to maintain for the resource to stay used, and who paid for that maintenance?
hook: A talk on open science practices that turn a project into a resource the community keeps using.

title: GEMS-Taiwan judging session
why: The twenty-five minutes the whole year is graded on. All three in the room. Nothing is scheduled against it and nothing may be — it costs us AI × Drug Discovery and the manufacturability talk, and that is the right price.

title: AI × Drug Discovery
why: Runs across our own judging session. Dropped without discussion.
hook: How AI-designed gene therapies move from computer models to patients, and what it does to pipeline cost.

title: Your Design Works - Could It Become a Medicine?
why: Manufacturability and validation on the way to clinic. Runs across our judging session; dropped.
hook: What manufacturability, quality control and validation require to take an engineered therapy to clinic.

title: Judging debrief, while it is fresh
why: Thirty minutes to write down what the judges asked, in their words, before anyone reconstructs it. The single highest-value half hour of the trip for all three reports.

title: Fusing Living Biological Neurons with Silicon Chips
why: Friday's keynote, and instrumentation at its limit: living neurons wired onto silicon to make sensors that smell. Go together after the judging debrief — it is the one keynote that is purely about building a measuring device.
hook: Chips wiring living neurons onto silicon produce sensors that smell, for screening and healthcare.

title: Pharma & Synthetic Biology
why: Founders on turning platforms into medicines. First of the Friday afternoon Innovation run, which is the institutional-direction track nobody else is covering.
hook: Founders describe engineering antibodies and new drug design platforms into the next generation of medicines.

title: DNA Dilemmas: A Policy-Building Challenge
why: Ninety minutes building a governance framework, hands on. The only session in the programme that produces responsibility material you cannot read off a wiki.
ask: Where does DNA synthesis screening actually fail — the order, the sequence, or the customer?
hook: Learn how DNA synthesis screening works, then build a governance framework for a fictional country.

title: On call for booth H-17
why: Students run the booth; one instructor stays inside Pavilion 7 with a phone on. Gabriel's Friday afternoon is all in-hall anyway.

title: A guide to closing funding gap in women’s research: insights from our stakeholders
relevance: ** Technique to borrow — a parts-characterisation protocol for an awkward chassis, and a reason to re-express our CcaSR characterisation in more than one reporter.
why: On closing a funding gap in women's research.
hook: Interviews with experts and funders on why conditions affecting women attract little research money.

title: Why should we care about growing plants in space?
relevance: same space
why: Growing plants in space.
hook: Carriers protect symbiotic fungi from oxidative stress so plants can grow in space soil and on Earth.
clash: DNA Dilemmas: A Policy-Building Challenge

title: Water Pollution - Where does it come from and where does it go?
relevance: technique to borrow — calibration methodology, almost directly transferable to the OD600 channel.
why: Their talk is on water pollution, not the 3D-printed reader calibrated into fluorescein-equivalent units that we want. Go for the person, not the talk.
ask: How did you tie the 3D-printed reader to fluorescein-equivalent units, and what did it cost you in time?
hook: Two teams trace where PFAS, heavy metals and PAHs come from and how they affect health.
clash: Pharma & Synthetic Biology

title: Navigating Commercialization for Biodefense - Where Pandemic Preparedness, Biodefense and Mass-Market Products Overlap
why: Where public-good science and a mass-market product share the same bench. Our own cost claim sits on that line.
hook: Where pandemic preparedness, biodefense and consumer products share science, and what building there demands.

title: How SynBio Solves the Biggest Environmental Challenges
why: The village's own framing talk. Runs inside DNA Dilemmas; dropped.
hook: How microbes, plants and enzymes treat contaminated sites and cut pollution, with research under way.

title: The Other 99%: Engineering Non-Model Organisms
why: B. subtilis sits off the E. coli path, and this panel is about exactly the barriers that cost us a year.
ask: When a Gram-positive host will not secrete a heterologous enzyme, at what point do you stop engineering the signal peptide and change the host?
hook: Panellists weigh the promise and practical barriers of engineering organisms beyond E. coli and yeast.

title: Ethanol from Paper Waste: Enzymatic Breakdown of Plastic-Coated Containers for High-Efficiency Microbial Bioethanol Conversion
relevance: same space
why: Taiwanese, enzymatic breakdown of a waste stream.
hook: Engineered enzymes break plastic-coated paper into sugars that bacteria then ferment into bioethanol.
clash: Navigating Commercialization for Biodefense - Where Pandemic Preparedness, Biodefense and Mass-Market Products Overlap

title: Learning from/with/in the Living. A Typology of Biodesign Training Programs
why: A typology of training programmes and how expectations shape what students learn — good pipeline material, but it opens while DNA Dilemmas is still running. Dropped; ask the panellists for the typology by email.
hook: A typology of biodesign training programs and how differing expectations shape what students learn.

title: From Research to Impact: Building the Future of IP Transfer on Evidence
why: Why spinouts stall on IP agreements, and what one model changes about the terms. GEMS has no position on who owns what a student builds, and will need one.
ask: Who should hold the IP when the inventor is seventeen and the lab belongs to a school?
hook: Why European spinouts stall on IP agreements, and what a Berlin model changes about the terms.

title: STING: Small TnpB-based Innovative Nuclease toolkit for bacterial Genome editing
relevance: technique to borrow
why: A TnpB nuclease toolkit for bacterial engineering.
hook: Directed evolution widens the TAM range of a compact TnpB nuclease for lighter bacterial genome editing.
clash: The Other 99%: Engineering Non-Model Organisms

title: Microbes That Work in the Field, but Don’t Persist: Multilayered Biosafety for Agricultural Use
relevance: direct competitor — and the single most useful technique-to-borrow booth in the slice.
why: Same enzyme, same chassis, same unsolved problem: they surface-display ACC deaminase on B. subtilis with a Tat signal and a LysM anchor. The one team talk worth leaving an official session for.
ask: Did you ever measure activity of the displayed enzyme, or only that it is on the surface?
hook: Layered physical and biological containment keeps engineered soil microbes working without persisting.

title: What Will We Have Got Wrong About SynBio in 2040?
why: Two founding figures grading the field's promises. All three: it is the cheapest available calibration of how far our own claims are ahead of our evidence.
ask: Which promise in a student project should a judge refuse to reward?
hook: Two founding figures of synthetic biology forecast which of today's promises pay off by 2040.

title: When Bio Meets the Consumer - Novel Foods, Consumer SynBio and the Future of What We Eat, Wear and Use
why: Precision fermentation and climate-ready crops reaching actual buyers — the far end of the path our plant-stress work points down.
hook: Startups bringing precision fermentation and climate-ready crops to what people eat, wear and use.

title: Design and Characterization of AsLOV2 Optogenetic Protein
relevance: direct competitor on optogenetics; technique to borrow on light-delivery hardware. Treat the modelled "42.7% greater antigen transport" as a simulation output, not a measurement — the abstract says the model predicted it.
why: A second optogenetic system characterised end to end; a comparison for the CcaSR fold change that caps our green ladder.
ask: What fold change did you get, and over what induction window?
hook: Light-switchable AsLOV2 modules control bacterial phosphorylation to trigger a fish vaccine on demand.

title: Fel d 1 Eraser: A Pet‑Friendly Neutralizing spray that Enzymatically degrades Fel d 1
relevance: same space
why: An enzymatic consumer product — a route from a protein to something a person buys.
hook: An enzyme spray breaks down the cat allergen Fel d 1 without harming pets.

title: Bringing colours to life
why: A plant-focused synthetic biology venture, in our own domain, closing Friday in the Technology plaza.

hook: A short talk introducing a plant-focused synthetic biology venture.

relevance: ** Technique to borrow — degradation tagging as a safety dial, and modelling used to choose a promoter rather than to decorate one.

title: One Mission, Many Voices & Countless Connections

hook: How feedback from Puerto Rican communities reshaped a team's outreach and engagement strategy.

hook: A staged reading of the 1976 recombinant DNA hearings, then discussion on public voice in research.

title: Operation Outbreak Simulation

hook: An artist and a biotechnology researcher discuss a multi-year collaboration inside university labs.

why: When to raise and what early decision-makers assess. Runs against the Standards panel, which is closer to the award we are chasing. Dropped.

why: A synthesis-services company on RNA therapeutics. Outside our space, and it runs into the publishing workshop. Dropped.

why: Between the publishing workshop and the Git for Genomes talk he is in-hall the whole time, and it frees Chars for the 1976 restaging in Nucleus.
